piece: Reconcile the two soul ledgers that disagree by 53% — population-posts.json's cached roll-up against the statblocks that actually pay. W1-SOULS-r3.md §2.1 / §9 is the spec.
next_step: CONSUMPTION in the running engine, then downstream figures, INDEX gate row, blog line, commit.
ownership_note: game/data/world/population-posts.json is generated by tools/world/build-population.mjs, which W1-POPULATION owns and which is `complete`. I did not modify the generator — I re-ran it. tools/check-data.mjs and tools/gen-index.mjs were unclaimed by any live piece when I declared them.
contention: node tools/contention.mjs --gate read WAIT at start (5 instances, 5.11/core). Every ledger arm above is offline JSON arithmetic and needed no browser. Re-gated GO (2 instances, 3.50/core) before the CONSUMPTION leg; one browser launched and kept.
findings: TRUTH = the statblocks. game/src/sim/souls.js awardFor(stat, awardHour) reads Engine.data.enemies[e.id].souls on the alive->dead transition and adds it to sim.progression.soulsHeld. It is the only producer of souls in the build and it never opens population-posts.json.
The cache has exactly one runtime reader: game/src/world/population.js report() -> souls_total = sum of post.souls, surfaced by __HARNESS.populationReport(). A reporting surface, not a payer.

Provenance corroborates the reading: population-posts.json last written at e54a18a 2026-08-07 18:50; the seven re-anchored statblocks written at 0c8acfa 22:36 and e97347f 00:50, i.e. AFTER. The cache is the older document.

RECONCILED by regenerating, not by hand-editing: node tools/world/build-population.mjs --write. The diff is souls-only — 144 posts, no post moved, no template changed, no body count changed; the only post field that differs anywhere is `souls`.
report.souls 16335 -> 10679 (the cache was +53.0%). crossing.souls 2149 -> 1404. crossing.level_if_fully_cleared 5 -> 3. All five by_tier and all twelve by_region soul rows corrected.
build-population.mjs --check already existed and already reported DRIFT, but it is wired into no gate, and being a byte-identity check it cannot name which number moved.
